candidates.attacker_control: The validated `CharSequence` is untrusted end-user rich text — precisely the input `@SafeHtml` is documented to defend ('Validate a rich text value provided by the user to ensure that it contains no malicious code', SafeHtml.java:28-37; default whitelistType RELAXED, SafeHtml.java:54). It is passed unmodified to Jsoup.parse/ Cleaner.isValid (SafeHtmlValidator.java:80,90); only a boolean is returned, so the attacker-controlled string itself still reaches the rendering sink in the application.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked `initialize()` (SafeHtmlValidator.java:37-72) — whitelist selection, additional tags/attributes/protocols are applied as documented, so configuration-side checks are not the weak point. Checked that jsoup presence is conditionally required (ConstraintHelper.java:323,724,1042-1044) — with jsoup absent the constraint is not registered (ConstraintValidatorManager would fail), so the vulnerable path requires the dependency, which the build declares (pom.xml:136; engine/pom.xml:91-94). Checked @SafeHtml javadoc/annotation (SafeHtml.java:28-73) — no documented limitation disclaiming responsibility for attribute/parser-difference bypasses. Checked that no output-side escaping/sanitization exists in the validator (isValid returns boolean only). Considered the alternative fix angle (that the constraint merely uses a flawed dependency and the source may be otherwise faithful to upstream 6.1.0-SNAPSHOT): the security defect is still the source's decision to base a security control on `Cleaner.isValid()` from a pinned 2014 jsoup, so it is reported as a source-level lead.
candidates.impact: Whitelist bypass of a security constraint shipped as part of Bean Validation metadata: attacker-supplied rich text that the application treats as sanitized can contain executable markup (event-handler attributes, script-bearing URLs, or parser-divergence payloads), giving stored/reflected cross-site scripting, session/credential theft, or defacement in applications that rely on @SafeHtml as their output-sanitization control. This is an integrity/confidentiality impact on users of the validating application rather than on the validator itself.
candidates.prerequisites: Application validates untrusted markup with `@SafeHtml` (default RELAXED or BASIC/BASIC_WITH_IMAGES etc.) and renders/stores the accepted raw value in an HTML context without separate output encoding. jsoup must be on the classpath for the constraint to be registered at all (ConstraintHelper.java:323,724,1042-1044) — in the WildFly-aligned setup this is jsoup 1.8.3 per pom.xml:136.
candidates.root_cause: SafeHtmlValidator.isValid(CharSequence, ConstraintValidatorContext) does not sanitize the value or compare the value with a sanitized equivalent; it returns `new Cleaner( whitelist ).isValid( getFragmentAsDocument( value ) )` (SafeHtmlValidator.java:80). getFragmentAsDocument (lines 86-100) parses the raw value with `Parser.xmlParser()`, then copies only `fragment.children()` (element children; top-level text and comments are silently dropped) into a brand-new shell document, so the verdict is taken on a *reconstructed* document, not on the user's string, and the raw string is left unchanged for the application to render. In addition, the build pins jsoup to 1.8.3 (pom.xml:136, engine/pom.xml:91-94, optional dependency, aligned with the supported WildFly), a 2014 release whose `Cleaner.isValid()` only determines whether cleaning retained the same number of top-level nodes and does not detect attributes removed by the whitelist (the 'discarded attributes' accounting was added in later jsoup releases). Any whitelist violation that does not change the top-level element count, or any difference between the XML parse used for validation and the browser's HTML parse of the rendered string, therefore yields 'valid' and the constraint's security guarantee is void.
candidates.title: @SafeHtml whitelist bypass: constraint delegates its verdict to jsoup Cleaner.isValid() on a rebuilt XML-parsed document (jsoup pinned at 1.8.3), allowing XSS payloads to validate
candidates.trace: (1) Untrusted value → SafeHtmlValidator.isValid (SafeHtmlValidator.java:75-81). (2) getFragmentAsDocument (lines 86-100) parses it with Parser.xmlParser(), drops non-element children, appends element children to a fresh Document.createShell body. (3) `new Cleaner(whitelist).isValid(document)` is the sole verdict; the cleaner's removals are (in the pinned jsoup 1.8.3) not reflected in the top-level node count, so stripped attributes (e.g. `onerror`/`onclick`, or a protocol-disallowed `href`) and nested/unsafe content can leave the count unchanged, and XML-parser structure can differ from the browser's HTML interpretation of the same raw bytes. (4) 'Valid' violates the constraint's purpose; the unmodified attacker string is stored/rendered → script execution / XSS.
candidates.unverified: jsoup itself is not in the snapshot, so the exact behaviour of 1.8.3's `Cleaner.isValid()` (node-count-only comparison, non-accounting of discarded attributes) was reasoned from the pinned version and the call site, not read here; no jsoup jar/source or test sources are present, and I did not execute any code. Therefore the precise minimal payload (attribute-only vs. XML/HTML parser-divergence form) is not demonstrated. Whether the upstream fix for this issue was a jsoup version bump (pom.xml) or a change inside SafeHtmlValidator.java could not be determined from the snapshot, which is why both locations are listed; no runtime confirmation of exploitability is claimed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation / XSS) via CWE-1104 use of an outdated, weak third-party sanitizer component

coverage_summary: Read-only review of the 928-file snapshot (source scope: 928 model-visible files, no binary exclusions, no symlinks; relation index: 928 files indexed, 6,935 symbols, 11,808 edges, index_status complete, no SAST/oracle data). Coverage concentrated on the attacker-facing surface of the engine (constraintvalidators/hv and bv, messageinterpolation incl. EL resolvers, xml parsers/config, metadata/ConstraintHelper registration, privilegedactions/reflection, valueextraction, properties), the CDI module (ValidationInterceptor, ValidatorFactoryBean, ValidationExtension), and the build/config files (root pom, engine/pom, modules/osgi/relocation). Test sources are entirely absent, and the annotation-processor module, the bulk of ValidatorImpl/ValidatorFactory internals, and groups/valueextraction were only spot-checked. The relation index was used only for navigation (its security_call/injection 'facts' proved to be generic keyword hits, e.g. `execute`/`checkPermission`/`readObject`), and every candidate was verified against source text after navigation.
limitations: All test sources and any jsoup sources/jars are excluded from the snapshot, so no test name, test resource or dependency source could corroborate the @SafeHtml/jsoup mechanism; findings rest on the call sites and the pinned dependency version (pom.xml:136).
No code was executed and no build/scanner was run (index states build_or_tests_run=false); exploitability of the reported whitelist bypass is not runtime-confirmed and no payload was fired.

Attribution of the defect to the pinned dependency vs. the validator's own logic could not be settled from the snapshot (no upstream history/patch available), hence both SafeHtmlValidator.java:74-101 and pom.xml:131-136 are listed as locations.

The bulk of the engine (large classes such as ValidatorImpl, ConstraintHelper internals, metadata aggregation, groups, valueextraction) was reviewed selectively, not line-by-line; a vulnerability there cannot be excluded.
The annotation-processor, OSGi/relocation/integration/distribution build files and the CDI extension internals were only partially inspected; absence of findings there reflects sampling, not proof.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE / missing DTD hardening in XML descriptor parsing: XmlParserHelper.java:57-96 creates `XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` without `XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false` / `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false`, and ValidationXmlParser.java:95-101 / MappingXmlParser.java:110-126 also run `SchemaFactory`-based `Validator.validate(StreamSource)` on the same stream without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD`/`ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions.
rejected_leads.reason: Real weakness, but attacker control is weak for this snapshot: the parsed documents are `META-INF/validation.xml` and constraint-mapping files loaded from the classpath or supplied programmatically by the deploying application (ResourceLoaderHelper.java:43-80), not remote input. No in-tree path where untrusted data reaches these parsers was found, so it does not meet the stronger-candidate threshold; noted as a hardening gap.

rejected_leads.lead: Script evaluation via @ScriptAssert / @ParameterScriptAssert (ScriptEngineScriptEvaluator.java:67 `engine.eval(script, bindings)`; DefaultScriptEvaluatorFactory.java:57-70 loads JSR-223 engines including from the TCCL).
rejected_leads.reason: Script source comes from annotation attributes (declaration-time, trusted) and the validated object is only exposed as bindings; this is documented behaviour, not an injection sink reachable by untrusted input.

rejected_leads.lead: Index hints to `execute(...)` in the annotation-processor (ClassVisitor.java:123, ConstraintAnnotationVisitor.java:209, MultiValuedChecks.java:42-50).
rejected_leads.reason: These are compile-time constraint-check dispatches, not process/command execution; the relation-index 'sql_or_process' label is a name-based heuristic and no security boundary or attacker input exists there.
No ObjectInputStream of untrusted data exists in the snapshot, and the class merely provides Java serialization support without any untrusted deserialization entry point.

rejected_leads.lead: EL interpolation of messages (ElTermResolver.java:62-112, AbstractMessageInterpolator.java:319-358) and removal of StaticFieldELResolver (SimpleELContext.java:24-33).
rejected_leads.reason: EL is evaluated on message templates from annotations/bundles (trusted); the value is only bound as a variable and interpolated values are escaped (PatternValidator.java:46, AbstractScriptAssertValidator.java:35 use InterpolationHelper.escapeMessageParameter). StaticFieldELResolver is already absent, so no stronger injection path was found.

summary: The snapshot is Hibernate Validator 6.1.0-SNAPSHOT (post-6.1.0.Alpha6, ~Oct 2019): 928 readable files, main sources of engine (592 internal files), cdi (19), annotation-processor, test-utils/performance, plus poms/config; all test sources are absent. The strongest plausible security issue is the `@SafeHtml` constraint path: `SafeHtmlValidator` makes its security verdict by handing a *reconstructed* document (parsed with jsoup's XML parser, only element children copied to a fresh shell) to `new Cleaner(whitelist).isValid(...)`, while the original, unsanitized value is what the application stores/renders; the constraint never sanitizes or compares the value against the sanitized output. The jsoup version pinned for this build is 1.8.3 (2014, also the WildFly-aligned version, optional dependency), whose `Cleaner.isValid()` is only a "does cleaning change the node count" check and does not account for attributes stripped by the whitelist. Consequently crafted input whose whitelist violations are attributes/nested or that diverges between XML and HTML parsing (e.g. event-handler attributes, protocol-restricted URLs such as `href="javascript:..."`, HTML-vs-XML comment/CDATA handling) can be reported valid, so untrusted input constrained with `@SafeHtml` can be persisted and later rendered as executable markup (stored/reflected XSS). No runtime confirmation was possible (no tests, no jsoup sources/jars in the snapshot), so this is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability. Other examined areas (EL interpolation hardening, SecurityManager-guarded reflection, XML config parsing, script evaluation, check-digit/URL/email validators) did not yield an equal-strength source-supported finding.
